**Verdict in brief:** Leadership is wrong about the mechanism, even if their discomfort with the pipeline is legitimate. Splitting the codebase doesn't shrink either of the two things actually bundled into the 45 minutes (full test-suite execution and coordinated restart) — it relocates that burden into more pipelines and adds new cross-service integration, versioning, and distributed-transaction overhead (CAP theorem, the fallacies of distributed computing) that a 12-person team isn't staffed to absorb (Google's SRE book puts a sustainable on-call minimum around 6–8 engineers per service — the team would be at 1.5–3 per service on a first-cut split). The recommendation: fix the pipeline in-monolith now (test parallelization, blue-green restart decoupling, feature flags — all independent of codebase architecture), modularize internally in parallel at low intensity, and defer any real service extraction until named, instrumented triggers (traffic divergence, on-call load, headcount) are actually met. Confidence: MEDIUM, capped mainly by one unverified fact — nobody has actually measured which stage of the pipeline dominates the 45 minutes — which the plan's first action is to resolve.
